provenance: Researched dossier with an explicitly reviewed identity match. Dates may follow a stated scholarly convention; source boundaries are independently attributed.
summary: A formally federal socialist state governed by the Communist Party that became a major industrial, military and diplomatic power.
currency: Soviet ruble; chervonets-denominated banknotes also circulated before the 1947 monetary reform.
rulers: Selected leader: Mikhail Gorbachev, 1985–1991; Communist Party general secretary until August 1991 and USSR president until December 1991.
economy: State ownership and central planning dominated much of its history; forced industrialization and collectivization transformed production at enormous human cost.
military: A nuclear superpower with large conventional forces, competing with the United States during the Cold War.
contributions: Launched the first artificial satellite, Sputnik 1, in 1957 and the first human into space, Yuri Gagarin, in 1961.
origin: Bolshevik victory in civil war preceded the union of Russia, Ukraine, Belarus and the Transcaucasian federation in December 1922.
decline: Economic crisis, political reforms, republican independence movements and the failed August 1991 coup culminated in dissolution.
periodNote: 1922 marks formation of the USSR, distinct from the Bolshevik seizure of power in 1917. It dissolved in December 1991; it was formally a union, not a monarchy.

boundaryIdentityNotes.note: USSR is the Soviet Union. Keep only snapshots during 1922–1991. The 1920 USSR label predates the Union’s establishment and should be quarantined; it must not be used as a 1920 Soviet Union border.
